front: Three main functions of the skeleton?
notes: Skull: brain; ribcage: heart and lungs; vertebral column: spinal cord.

front: Bones of the mammalian forelimb, from the shoulder?
back: Scapula, humerus, radius and ulna (then carpals, metacarpals, phalanges).

front: Bones of the mammalian hindlimb, from the hip?
back: Pelvic girdle, femur, tibia and fibula (then tarsals, metatarsals, phalanges).
Elbow and knee; movement in one plane (bending and straightening).
Shoulder and hip; movement in all directions, including rotation.
Ligament: joins bone to bone, slightly elastic. Tendon: joins muscle to bone, inelastic.

front: Roles of cartilage and synovial fluid in a joint?
back: Cartilage reduces friction and absorbs shocks; synovial fluid lubricates.
A pair of muscles producing opposite movements at a joint: when one contracts, the other relaxes.
notes: Needed because muscles can only pull.

front: What happens when the arm bends at the elbow?
back: The biceps (flexor) contracts and pulls the radius; the triceps relaxes.

front: What happens when the arm straightens?
back: The triceps (extensor) contracts and pulls the ulna; the biceps relaxes.
